s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging, red, cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule on the upper arm
salient_findings: red tumor on the right upper arm
key_facts: 16-year-old girl
previously healthy
lesion started as a small cutaneous nodule
enlarged over 6 months
no history of local trauma or insect bite
unremarkable personal, past, and family histories
6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red tumor
nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor
normal laboratory tests
normal physical and systemic examinations
multilocular spaces below the epidermis on pathological examination
solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance

shortlist.label: Pilomatrixoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical description of a firm, cutaneous nodule with a chalky-white appearance

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: possible given the firm-to-hard nodule and normal laboratory tests

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the rapid growth and cutaneous location of the tumor

shortlist.label: Pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the red, protuberant tumor with a hard nodule

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of a firm-to-hard nodule and normal laboratory tests

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, along with the description of a solid tumor with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance, are characteristic features of pilomatrixoma.

rejected.label: Dermatofibroma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a firm, brownish to purple nodule, often following trauma, which does not match the patient's history or the tumor's description.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Usually appears as a solitary, firm, round nodule with a central crater filled with keratin, which is not consistent with the multilocular spaces and solid tumor described.

rejected.label: Pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a rapidly growing, bleeding, red nodule, often following trauma, which does not fit the patient's history of a gradually enlarging tumor without trauma.

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents as a painful, blue-purple nodule under the nail or on the fingertips, which does not match the location or description of the tumor in this case.
